grades.quote: All message interrupts adopt a uniform entry, and the "entry page number" of their computed entry address coincides with the line interrupt, coming from an "in-page offset" equal to 2(CSR.ECFG.VS+2)×78(0x4E) of their computed entry address.
grades.reason: Explains how the entry address is formed for LoongArch message interrupts. They share a uniform entry. The page number matches the line interrupt, and the in-page offset depends on CSR.ECFG.VS. This covers only message interrupts, not exceptions in general.

grades.quote: The subsequent process of the processor is the same as that of the general exception, see the description in General Hardware Exception Handling of General Exceptions.
grades.reason: Describes how the processor decides an interrupt must be taken (ESTA.IS AND ECFG.LIE, CRMD.IE). It then defers to general exception handling. It does not say how the handler entry address is selected, so it is only auxiliary context.

grades.quote:
The RNMI interrupt trap handler address is implementation-defined.

RNMI also has an associated exception trap handler address, which is implementation defined.
grades.reason: Covers only the RNMI (Smrnmi) case. The interrupt and exception handler addresses are implementation-defined, and the passage hints that an implementation might use mtvec. It gives no general selection mechanism based on configuration or trap type.
